newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end week strong in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end week strong in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares traded largely firm in an active market on Friday with brokers predicting the bourse would continue strong on a fresh wave of local institutional buying.
"The market is looking good. We expect it to continue on an upward trend and everybody expects it to pick up the bullish trend when the rains come, if they look good," one broker said.
The 57-industrial index jumped 41.93 points to close at 6.990.32 -- a leap of 236.93 points on the week.

It was driven up mainly by finance group Finhold's 75-cent rise to 1,000, cement producer Porthold's 50-cent climb to 1,300, tobacco firm TSL's 30-cent gain to 560 and finance house UDC's 20-cent addition to 240.
Pharmaceutical group Caps and pork processor Colcom put on 10 cents each to 250 and 320 respectively while textiler Spinweave and hotel chain Zimsun both traded at previous levels.
Against the trend, bankers Barclays at 1,990, rubber products manufacturer FSI at 200 and steel window and door producer Radar at 190 all shed 10 cents.

Minings were quieter on a softer gold price on overseas markets. Falgold traded unchanged at 175 while gold producer Ashanti leapt 200 cents to 15,500 and Wankie Colliery added 10 cents to 360. Nickel firm Bindura dropped 75 cents to 1,150.
The seven-stock mining index gained 9.96 points to close at 1,363.07 -- a loss of 5.87 points on the week.
